findings.title: Structured-body schema completion lacked a positive regression
findings.claim: The structured-body path did not test that a genuinely missing schema-required H2 stub is appended with canonical spacing.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the adjacent mutation regression with one omitted required section and exact spacing assertions.
findings.evidence: The original regression supplied every required section. It now requires an omitted Quick Test section and proves exactly one correctly separated stub is appended.

findings.title: Agent guidance overstated default epic rendering
findings.target_symbol: Action: Create / Flesh out the body
findings.claim: The agent template categorically said the CLI never writes epic sections although repository schema requirements can append those stubs.
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the statement as default-renderer behavior in both templates and dogfooded copies.
findings.evidence: do_new_locked appends configured required sections after rendering. The four agent-facing files now distinguish default rendering from schema completion.

findings.title: Issuectl JSON export-to-import duplicates structured body headings
findings.claim: Issuectl JSON export body aliases to free-text import description and receives another generated Description wrapper when rendered.
findings.suggested_fix: Design separate structured body versus free-text description import handling and add an end-to-end round-trip regression.
findings.write_up:
- **Milloin tämä näkyy käyttäjälle** — kun käyttäjä vie issuectl-issuet JSON-muotoon ja tuo saman JSON-aineiston takaisin `issuectl import` -komennolla.
- **Miten se näkyy** — tuotu body käsitellään vapaana kuvauksena, joten jo rakenteisessa bodyssa oleva `## Description` saa eteensä uuden samannimisen otsikon; myös vanha H1 voi jäädä uuden otsikon alle.
- **Miksi sillä on väliä** — työkalun oma JSON-vienti on dokumentoitu importin syötteeksi, mutta uudelleentuonti voi rikkoa bodyn rakenteen jokaisessa tietueessa.
- **Miksi tämä vaatii oman suunnittelunsa** — parserin pitää erottaa issuectl-exportin rakenteinen `body` ulkoisten lähteiden vapaasta `description`-tekstistä rikkomatta GitHub- ja käsin kirjoitettujen importtien nykyisiä semantiikkoja.
- Korjaus tarvitsee erilliset yhteensopivuustestit koko export → parse → create -ketjulle; tämän create-only-korjauksen vaatimus nimenomaisesti säilyttää importin nykyisen käytöksen.
findings.evidence: Issue.body serializes as body; ImportRecord aliases body into description; into_new_args sets free-text mode. The existing round-trip test stops after parse and does not render the imported record.

findings.title: Changelog entry should move from Fixed to Changed
findings.claim: The corrected body-file semantics must be classified as Changed rather than Fixed in the changelog.
findings.evidence: The entry precisely describes correction of the reported duplicate-heading bug. Keep a Changelog permits persisted behavior corrections under Fixed; no repository rule requires Changed here.

findings.title: Heading-less structured bodies must warn or error
findings.claim: A structured body without H2 headings must warn or error, especially when schema completion appends a missing Description stub.
findings.evidence: Markdown body content need not contain H2 headings, and the declared mode intentionally places supplied content as-is. Schema completion correctly appends sections that are absent; sniffing would invent a second implicit mode grammar.

findings.title: Boolean body mode permits contradictory core states
findings.claim: Option description plus structured_body bool permits None plus true and requires callers to coordinate a cross-field invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the body fields with an InitialBody enum.
findings.evidence: The type can represent None plus true, but every current constructor is explicit and correct and the CLI rejects empty files. An enum refactor would coordinate owned and borrowed argument shapes without demonstrated production failure.

findings.title: Trailing Markdown whitespace is lost by the new structured mode
findings.claim: The structured-body change newly loses Markdown-significant trailing whitespace.
findings.evidence: Trailing document whitespace normalization predates this diff, is explicitly documented, and is shared with body replacement. Interior-line Markdown hard breaks remain intact.

findings.title: Schema stubs lack a separating blank line
findings.claim: Appending missing schema sections places the heading directly against preceding structured-body text.
findings.evidence: The append path checks for one and then two terminal newlines before adding stubs. The expanded regression directly verifies canonical separation.

findings.title: Canonical frontmatter splitting is a no-op
findings.claim: item_text::split is ineffective because the rendered string has no frontmatter.
findings.evidence: render_new_item_from_fm serializes and prepends YAML frontmatter. Gemini retracted the claim in the final round.

findings.title: Templates drifted and a constructor field was missing
findings.claim: The final diff omitted synchronized template copies and structured_body initialization in cli_tests.rs.
findings.evidence: The complete tree contains both templates, both dogfooded copies, and the test constructor field. OpenAI retracted claims caused by a reduced cross-round attachment set.

findings.title: Compatibility paths should adopt structured mode
findings.claim: Intake, recurrence, core API, or foreign imports should switch to structured mode as part of this patch.
findings.evidence: The task explicitly requires those paths to preserve free-text semantics. Their false assignments are deliberate and architecture-consistent compatibility choices.

findings.title: Structured body files need an H1 prohibition
findings.claim: Create should reject or warn when structured body content includes its own H1.
findings.evidence: A supplied H1 is accepted beneath the generated title, but no observed occurrence or harmful ambiguity was demonstrated. Validation would add a new content restriction for a rare misuse.

findings.title: Create should reject unclosed Markdown fences
findings.claim: Structured create body input should reject an unclosed code fence before schema stubs are appended.
findings.evidence: The path does not validate fence balance, but this is pre-existing acceptance of malformed user Markdown. No real-world occurrence was shown and adding rejection broadens the CLI contract.

findings.title: Required headings should support broader CommonMark forms
findings.claim: Schema-required section detection should accept additional CommonMark-equivalent H2 forms.
findings.evidence: The repository deliberately uses canonical exact H2 section names across formatting, schema, and doctor behavior. Broadening the grammar is cross-cutting hardening without a demonstrated occurrence.

findings.title: Duplicate precheck must score the rendered body
findings.claim: Duplicate precheck using supplied content rather than generated heading boilerplate materially mis-scores structured bodies.
findings.evidence: The precheck intentionally scores semantic supplied content, and no failing score or user-visible regression was demonstrated. Generated title/source/wrapper tokens need not improve duplicate quality.

findings.title: Body-file integration test needs renaming
findings.claim: The integration test name no longer describes wrapper-free body-file behavior.
findings.evidence: The test still verifies exactly what its name states: Markdown from a body file is written below the generated heading. The name does not promise a Description wrapper.

findings.title: Touched epic guidance recommended a reserved legacy section
findings.claim: The edited agent guidance recommended ## Notes although Notes is a reserved legacy alias whose canonical replacement is ## Comments.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace Notes with Comments in both templates and rendered dogfooded copies.
findings.evidence: LEGACY_SECTION_ALIASES maps Notes to Comments and create help warns on Notes. All four agent artifacts now use Comments and the dogfood synchronization test passes.

findings.title: CLI-to-schema composition lacked a black-box regression
findings.claim: Separate tests covered CLI mode propagation and core schema completion but not their complete built-binary composition.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a CLI integration test with structured body, horizontal rule, present required headings, and one missing appended stub.
findings.evidence: The new integration test invokes the binary and proves exactly one of each required section plus canonical append ordering after the horizontal rule.

findings.title: CLI help omitted schema-appended stubs
findings.claim: The create body-file help did not disclose that repository schemas can append missing required H2 stubs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same schema-completion qualification used by the shipped agent template.
findings.evidence: Create help now states that repository schema requirements may append stubs for missing H2 sections.
